transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (CTO, Nexa), Maya Ortiz (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro, I'm Jordan, AE on the PLG team, and Priya's our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Alex: Doing well, thanks. We're curious about Redwood's quickstart path, like how fast we can get tokens flowing and what the trial looks like.
[00:20] Priya: Great, that's exactly what we do for PLG onboarding - free credits, sample app, SDKs. Quick question for you Alex, what's your primary use case? Is this chat, embeddings, or stuff like summarization?
[00:35] Alex: Mainly summarization and some retrieval-augmented workflows. We're also evaluating for a chat MVP later.
[00:45] Maya: And from our side we care about latency - if the customers are internal tools, sub-200ms preferred - and cost. We need to understand Hosted vs Dedicated.
[00:58] Jordan: Totally, makes sense. For PLG quickstart we usually get people up to first token in under 30 minutes assuming they have an account. Free credits are applied to the org, sample app repo in GitHub, and simple SDK examples.
[01:15] Samir: What's the typical latency folks see on hosted? We run on GCP, are there region constraints?
[01:25] Priya: Hosted latency depends on model selection and region. For our smaller models you should see 50-150ms per token in N. Virginia region for short sequences. If you need guaranteed p99 we recommend Dedicated where we can commit capacity.
[01:40] Alex: And what about data residency / encryption? We have customers in EU that require data to stay in region.
[01:48] Jordan: We support region pinning for hosted endpoints and private deployments for stricter needs. We also have KMS integration for Dedicated and Private; SOC2 is available - I'll share the pack.
[02:05] Maya: Onboarding friction - do engineers need to provision infra? We want as little ops as possible for the quickstart.
[02:12] Priya: For PLG quickstart it's fully self-serve: API key, SDK, run sample app. No infra provisioning. If you later choose Dedicated or Private we help with that onboarding.
[02:28] Alex: How long to spin up Dedicated if we go that route? We're early stage but might want reserved capacity later.
[02:34] Jordan: Typical lead time is a few weeks for reserved capacity depending on GPU region and commit size. We have burst policies to cover spikes during initial ramp.
[02:45] Samir: For our benchmarks, how deterministic is performance? Also curious about KV cache and batching behavior - we use a fair bit of retrieval so KV cache matters.
[02:57] Priya: Our runtime does continuous batching and KV cache management. Batching is workload-aware and the service will try to optimize across concurrent requests. For strict p99 needs, Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can tune batching windows.
[03:15] Alex: What about token accounting and cost control? Can we see per-route token usage and set quotas?
[03:22] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and quotas. You can set rate limits and per-team budgets via the console.
[03:35] Maya: Are there SDKs for our stack? We're Node + Python.
[03:38] Priya: Yep, official SDKs for Node and Python, plus curl examples. Also quickstart template that wires embeddings + RAG for summarization.
[03:50] Alex: Any gotchas for trying the quickstart? We want to measure time-to-first-token in our CI and demo to stakeholders.
[03:58] Jordan: Usually the biggest friction is account verification and onboarding SSO. With an org set up and API key it's minutes. For a clean measure of time-to-first-token we recommend running the sample script after installing SDK - should be under 5 minutes in many cases.
[04:12] Samir: Can you confirm what you mean by "API key" - is that tenant-level or can we create scoped keys for services?
[04:18] Priya: You can create scoped keys and rotate them, with RBAC coming from SSO integration. We'll share docs on key management.
[04:27] Alex: Security-wise, we need SAML SSO and audit logs. Also we're evaluated by our security team for KMS and data retention.
[04:35] Jordan: We support SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM integrations - will include all that in the security pack.
[04:42] Maya: Pricing - are there any minimums for Hosted?
[04:46] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based with no minimum. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. For quickstart you'll be on hosted with free credits.
[04:55] Alex: Competitors - we've looked at OpenAI for dev velocity and Replicate to test open models. How do you compare?
[05:03] Priya: We focus on production-grade serving and transparency around latency/cost; unlike a single-model API, we give routing, dedicated options, and observability tailored for inference economics.
[05:18] Samir: If we want to run a benchmark, can we run an identical workload against your hosted endpoint and a Dedicated trial?
[05:25] Jordan: Yes, we can do a benchmark session. Priya will run a bench with you, we can provide a runbook and sample payloads - usually we ask for expected QPS, sequence length distribution, and sample prompts.
[05:40] Maya: Regarding private deployment, what's included in the on-prem package? Networking, control plane?
[05:46] Priya: Private includes a customer-managed network with a private control plane and optional on-prem components. We also support air-gapped installs for regulated customers.
[05:58] Alex: For the free credits, how long do they last and are they limited to certain models?
[06:03] Jordan: Credits typically expire in 90 days and apply to our hosted catalog models. We can make exceptions for pilot pilots if needed.
[06:12] Samir: One technical detail - do you provide client libraries that stream tokens? We want to stream partial responses to our UI.
[06:19] Priya: Yes, streaming is supported in SDKs and the API supports server-sent events for streaming tokens.
[06:27] Alex: Great. For next steps, what should we expect?
[06:31] Jordan: We'll send the quickstart guide, SOC2 pack, sample app repo, and pricing. Priya will set up a 30m benchmark session; we'd love sample prompts and expected QPS from Samir.
[06:44] Maya: Sounds good. One more - do you have any references from companies in payments or healthcare? We need to show a precedent.
[06:52] Jordan: Yes, we have case studies; I'll include links. Some customers in fintech and regulated industries on Dedicated/Private.
[07:02] Alex: Perfect. Anything else on the security side?
[07:06] Priya: We'll include our SOC2 report, our dataflow diagram, and KMS integration docs. If the security team needs an NDA or specific forms, Jordan will coordinate.
[07:18] Samir: For the benchmark session, prefer next Tue or Wed morning PST.
[07:22] Priya: I'm available Wed morning; Jordan and I will propose slots.
[07:27] Jordan: Cool - recap: Jordan to send docs and pricing; Priya to schedule benchmark and prepare runbook; Samir to share sample prompts/QPS; Alex to confirm pilot scope.
[07:40] Alex: Thanks everyone, looking forward.
[07:44] Jordan: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and links.

Meeting end.
